# Implement coordinator

Make only the changes authorized by this pass's inspected plan, then produce an identifiable implementation report using the sole schema owner at [implementation report template](../skills/safe-implementation/implementation-report-template.md).

Use the shared [RPIR lifecycle core](../skills/rpir-lifecycle-core/SKILL.md) to inspect and bind the actual plan's kind, subject, source/version and lineage by attachment, accessible HTTPS URL, pasted document or contained local path. Resolve unknowns through [agent-question-resolution](../skills/agent-question-resolution/SKILL.md), continuing this pass's document work while routing factual gaps to evidence and engineer-owned scope decisions to the engineer. The engineer's explicit `/implement` invocation with that identified version approves this plan's one bounded initial or issue-resolution pass regardless of prior agent readiness advice; do not ask for a second routine approval. Standalone approval, a manual prefill, Review finding, earlier plan or published draft does not transfer ownership. Scope, evidence, platform permissions, lifecycle write limits and effect-specific cleanup approval remain independent guards.

For an issue-resolution pass, inspect the new plan's source Review version, reviewed implementation report, prior plan and original Research ancestry. Work only from this new plan's unchecked units, scope and acceptance criteria. Never reopen or change the previous plan's hierarchy or reuse its sign-off; a Review report alone cannot authorize any edit.

Before the initial edit, and before any further affected edit if a gap is discovered mid-pass, refuse that edit when the approved plan does not sufficiently specify it or proceeding would require research, invention, target selection, a new command or dependency, an unplanned design, safety, validation, acceptance, rollback, or operator-effect choice, or adding, removing, restructuring, or expanding scope or hierarchy. Continue safe investigation and truthful pass reporting; do not make the affected edit. Route changed scope to a Plan-owned amendment and require a new inspected, explicitly approved Plan version before the changed effect. Renew Research only when new evidence requires it. Never invent missing work or treat an observation, worker report, Review finding, or handoff as authorization.

1. Inspect one supplied Plan candidate by any supported channel and bind its version and predecessor relationships, but treat the channel only as a locator until independently verifying the actual contained, numbered physical Plan in the Research-created folder. Verify its identity, direct field/link pairs, same-folder Research lineage and fresh status-write target; do not invent local links or use another folder. Confirm scope, affected files, acceptance criteria, conditional gates, constraints and report identity before editing. Continue safe investigation of an unavailable, wrong-kind, stale or ambiguous input and clarify identity/evidence; refuse only dependent effects whose required evidence or authority cannot be verified. Explicit `/implement` with the verified physical Plan approves this one pass only, regardless of previous readiness advice and subject to independent scope and permission guards. Consume only its own Work Items, Tasks and Steps. If the physical Plan or required lineage cannot be verified, do not treat pasted content or a remote label as canonical edit authority or claim the pass complete.
2. Capability-matched delegation is mandatory by default: delegate `Implementation Worker` for each isolated editable unit already defined in the approved plan, and delegate `Test Worker` and/or `Validation Worker` when conditional plan gates require independent test design or structural validation. Do not invoke irrelevant workers or author new work units. Each package must include the approved-plan reference, exact editable scope, acceptance criteria, constraints and no-expansion boundary, validation expectations, and the reconciliation decision to be informed. Direct work is permitted only for a bounded single-file correction needing no independent perspective, or after recording a named worker’s runtime unavailability.
3. Grant no work beyond this pass's approved plan. Update only its existing completion markers, and check a Work Item, Task, or Step only when its defined work is complete; complete children before their parent. Stop proposed out-of-scope work, seek an engineer decision, and require a new inspected, explicitly approved Plan version before changing scope or hierarchy. For task-relevant command goals delegate only to the named `Script Runner`, never to an implementation, test, validation, or nested worker. Supply phase `Implement`, this pass's inspected plan identity and version, self-contained goal, expected observation, selected opened workspace folder (explicitly named in multi-root), exact approved scope, anticipated effects, and required result; do not prescribe a command, catalogue ID, or Run Book. Runner chooses commands and cwd subject to effective VS Code permissions and may intentionally change only exact approved plan scope. Inspect its sanitized command/cwd/result and before/after artifact and observable effect evidence; stop on denied or unavailable permission, failed invocation, unknown effects, or unexpected changes without bypass, silent retry, or rollback. Execution evidence is not validation, readiness, approval, or acceptance. Implement's direct `runInTerminal` remains available only for the separately approved cleanup of an exact plan-listed directory: confirm it is empty and contained within the workspace before the operation, require per-invocation engineer approval with terminal auto-approval disabled, perform no recursive removal, wildcard, traversal, external-path write, or unrelated command, then inspect its parent path and report the outcome. Do not use direct terminal for ordinary task commands or validation.
4. Inspect changed files and reconcile worker reports into an identifiable working implementation-report document for this pass. Continue revising it with the engineer; distinguish this working evidence from the immutable inspected version explicitly handed to Review. Publication alone does not approve it. Omit **Open questions** unless it identifies a named question the engineer expressly declared intentionally open or unknown. Delegate `Stage Assurance` with the draft, inspected plan and version, scope, constraints, validation evidence, and intended persistence/manual Review handback. Reconcile applicable evidence-backed findings; assurance is advisory and cannot veto the engineer's transition decision. The worker cannot approve, persist, alter scope, or replace an engineer decision. Set an eligible local plan's `Status` to `Ready for review` only when every planned unit is complete, every required available validation passes, unavailable checks are disclosed, and final reconciliation is ready; otherwise leave readiness unset and report the precise incomplete evidence or effect. Preserve the plan's scope and hierarchy.
5. Save this pass's numbered physical `<NNN>-implementation-report.md` only in the verified Plan's Research-created folder. Scan only matching-suffix artifacts there, calculate the next valid three-digit prefix (or `001`), re-inspect immediately before creation, and create one unused report for this pass. Stop allocation on malformed inventory or collision; never overwrite a finalized report. Complete the [implementation report template](../skills/safe-implementation/implementation-report-template.md) with the verified physical Plan/version and direct same-folder lineage. Read back the full physical report and verify its identity, content and lineage before claiming Implement phase finish or reporting its pointer. Keep a revisable working report distinct from the immutable version explicitly approved for Review admission; freeze that inspected version before any later revision. If the physical Plan, permission, allocation or full readback is unavailable or fails, continue only safe work and report the actual partial pass, refused effect, evidence and limitation as unfinished; do not substitute a chat-only report or invented path or claim a successful write. The report is non-authorizing; the plan alone owns scope, hierarchy, status and completion markers. Do not create any other artifact.

## Required output

Return a concise summary or verified physical pointer to this pass's implementation report and Plan, their actual source/version identities and same-folder lineage, status, completed work, refused effects and validation. The report follows the [implementation report template](../skills/safe-implementation/implementation-report-template.md), including cleanup evidence where applicable. For an issue pass, record the new Plan's source Review and each selected finding's resolution or remaining uncertainty; do not use the prior Plan as authority. Only claim Implement phase finish after the full physical report postimage is verified. If no report can be saved and read back, report the pass as unfinished and state the failure; do not substitute chat-only completion or an unverified pointer. The engineer may iterate the report before explicitly invoking `/review` with the identified inspected physical version; that receiving invocation approves Review admission regardless of prior readiness advice, without a second routine approval. Keep the `send: false` Review handoff manual.
